newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed with losses but above session lows after tracking an early slide in bunds triggered by the row over the revaluation of Bundesbank gold.
The Finance Ministry closed tap sales of the second tranche of its 5.75 percent February 2007 bond after raising 5.0 billion guilders over three days.
Dealers said the gold dispute between the Bundesbank and the Bonn government had added to worries about the strength of the single European currency, the euro, due to be launched in 1999.

Dealers said the rise in 10-year Dutch yields to over 5.80 percent had lured some domestic buyers, especially now some fund managers had doubts about the durability of the bull market in Dutch equities with the AEX share index stalled around 800.

New figures today showed Dutch GDP grew at an underlying year-on-year rate of 3.0 percent in the first quarter of 1997 after stripping out the effect of an extra leap-year day in 1996 which drove down the headline growth figure to 2.1 percent.
This was seen as confirming that potential inflationary pressures in the Netherlands are greater than in Germany which in turn is seeing limiting scope for Dutch outperformance.
